name: Hermes-designed explainer page
description: Research only: Hermes writes the HTML page for each video from this brief, the owner approves still frames, then the worker captures it.

cautions: Research only: a video from a page Hermes wrote is never published.
Write the argument yourself. Don't paraphrase another channel's script or copy a specific channel's look.

design.brief: A calm flat-vector explainer for a portrait short: one idea per scene, built step by step. Each scene states its point in a short heading, then one simple animated element makes it concrete (a bar that grows, a counter, an arrow, a small diagram drawn with SVG or CSS). Every scene enters within its first 0.5 s and settles by the middle, so the narration has a still picture to land on; the first scene shows its point within 3 s. Scenes follow the scene list you return, in order, with hard cuts at the scene times. Draw only what the script says; numbers on screen must be ones the script states.
design.typography: Headings in 'Inter Tight' 700 and labels in 'Inter' 500, both from ../pack/fonts/fonts.css (vendored, SIL OFL 1.1); or the run's font when props.font is set. At least 6% of the short side for headings and 3.5% for labels. Sentence case, at most 8 words a heading.
design.layout: 1080x1920 portrait. Keep 8% margins on the left and right. The worker burns the captions at the bottom: draw nothing that matters below 70% of the height. Headings sit in the top third; the animated element in the middle third. Alternate a light scene (#F4EFE6 background, #1F2A44 ink) and a dark one (#1F2A44 background, #F4EFE6 ink); accents #E4572E, #2E86AB, #F6AE2D, #5BC0BE, one or two per scene.

provenance.notes: The look this brief describes: calm narrator, flat illustration, one tight argument built step by step.
